From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 19 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Execution lane & acceptance ladder — MAP + evaluation sprint for Solstice Bank

Hi Emily — thanks again for signing. Attaching the first draft of the Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that embeds the post-signature implementation commitments: rollout windows, canary guardrails, migration steps, and the 3-week training cadence.

High level asks for this week:
- Please confirm the preferred go-live week window (we proposed 10/01–10/07).
- Confirm who will own traffic shaping during canary (app infra or platform ops).
- Share any blackout dates between Sept 24–Oct 7.

Attached: MAP_Solstice_v1.xlsx (MAP with lane owners), Eval_Prompts_v1.csv (initial prompt set for quality/regen tests), SOW_appendix_A.pdf (noted acceptance criteria).

Proposed canary plan (summary):
1) Canary day 0–3: 1% production traffic, automated quality checks against eval set every hour.
2) Canary day 4–7: 10% traffic with manual checkpoint review; rollback window nightly.
3) Full ramp by day 14 if acceptance ladder metrics met.

Acceptance ladder (examples):
- Latency P95 below 450ms for 1-token average path.
- Regression on eval prompt set < 2% in top-1 adequacy drop compared to baseline model.
- Error rate (server errors + timeouts) < 0.2%.

We included a short training plan for your product and support teams (two 90-minute sessions + office hours for 2 weeks). Marissa will run the enablement schedule. Jonas will lead the canary instrumentation checklist.

Link to living MAP/drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-Solstice-MAP

If that looks acceptable I can push a finalized MAP and calendar invites by EOD Monday.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com
(415) 555-0143

Thanks Rachel — appreciate the speed. A few quick items from our side:
- Go-live window: prefer 10/08–10/14 (we have a product release the week before). Can you shift the ramp by one week?
- Traffic owner: Platform Ops (Tom Nguyen) will own traffic steering during canary; cc'd.
- Blackout: none besides an internal maintenance on 9/29 that should not affect the chosen window.

Procurement asked for the MAP table in XLSX (good) and a separate one-page acceptance checklist that procurement can attach to the contract. Can you include that as a short PDF?

Finally, the eval prompt set looks good, but we need a sample of simulated traffic patterns (1000 request/hour burst and a 10k/day baseline) so our SOC team can review rate-limiter configs.

Best,
Emily
